dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Sandra. Good morning, how can I help you?
Hi. Um, good morning. I'm calling about a noise thing. A bar. The music from a bar. [pause] Sorry, I don't even know if this is the right office.
You're fine, honey, this is a good place to start. Which bar are we talking about, and where is it?

It's, well, I'm at 69 Carroll Avenue, in the Fifth Ward. That's where I live and where I have my shop, downstairs. And the bar is a few blocks over. I'm not going to say it's right next door, because it isn't. That's the thing. I can hear the bass from here. Blocks away.
Blocks away. Wow. Is it live music or a DJ, do you know?

I think it's a band, maybe a DJ, honestly I can't tell. It's just thump, thump, thump through the walls. [pause] It's been three days now. Sunday night, Monday night, and last night. Last night went past midnight, I looked at the clock, it was like twelve forty.
Oh, that's no good, especially on a Tuesday. And you said you've got a shop. Do you have to be up early for that?

Yeah, I open at seven. I'm doing inventory and orders and everything by myself, so when I don't sleep it's just, [sighs] it's a long day. Sorry. I'm rambling. I really just wanted to ask a simple question.
No, ramble away, it's a quiet morning. What's the question?

What are the quiet hours? Like, is there an actual time when they have to turn it down? Because I looked on the website and I couldn't find it, or I found about four different pages and none of them said it plainly. And the thing is, I don't even want to get anybody in trouble, I just want to know if midnight is, you know, a reasonable thing to expect. Sorry, I'm doing it again.

You're all right. So generally the city has limits on loud noise late at night, and entertainment at licensed establishments has its own conditions on the license. I don't want to hand you the wrong exact hour, so let me tell you who has that. The police handle noise when it's happening, and the license conditions are tracked through our office.
Okay. So if it's going at midnight, I call the police? For music? That feels like a lot.

Their non-emergency line, not 911. That's what it's for. They can go over, listen, and tell the bar to turn it down. And separately I can log your complaint here so there's a record, especially since it's three nights running. A record matters if it keeps up and the license comes up for review.
Yeah, please do that. I'd rather it be on file. I just don't want to be the person who calls every night. But I also can't keep doing this.
Totally fair. Let me get this down. Your name?
Isabel Silva. S-I-L-V-A.
Thank you, Isabel. And 69 Carroll Avenue, that's where you're hearing it. Do you know the name of the bar, or the street it's on?

I think it's the one down by the corner, off Thames maybe? I'm not a hundred percent sure of the name. I can tell you it's not close, which is what's so strange. Everything's just carrying. It must be the way the sound goes down the street.
Could be, sound does odd things near the water. I'll note the general direction and the nights, Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday, going past midnight. If you find out the name, call back and I'll add it.
Okay. Yeah, I'll look tonight. Or, I mean, I'll hear it tonight, probably.
Hopefully not. Is the number you're on the best one to reach you?
Yes, 401-555-0181. That's the shop line, it's the landline, so I'm usually here.
Got it. Someone from the office will follow up on the license side, and if it starts up again, call the police non-emergency line right then so they hear it live.
Okay. Alright. Thank you. Sorry again for going on.
Not at all. Try to get some rest, Isabel. Take care now.
You too. Bye.
